report.summary: 1. CHEAP fitness signals: Trivial Compiler Equivalence (TCE) by Le Goues et al. (2012) uses compiler optimizations; GenProg uses test suite only. 2. Behavioural descriptors: AST-based novelty (Forrest et al., 2009) works; output-only novelty fails for programs. 3. Equivalent mutant rate: ~10-40% (Jia & Harman, 2011); bounded by compiler-based detection (TCE) or manual review. 4. Failure modes: overfitting to pre-test signal, missing semantic changes, high false positives for complex refactors.
risks: Pre-test signal may reject valid patches that change structure without altering identifiers or constants.
High false-alarm rate for refactoring or dead code removal.
44% miss rate may be partly due to equivalent mutants (10-40%), but remaining miss is real.
todos: Compare false-alarm rates with TCE on same dataset.
Evaluate behavioural descriptors for novelty search on program space.
Estimate equivalent mutant rate for your specific mutation operators.

handoff.suggestion: Consider combining AST delta with TCE for stronger cheap signal; use behavioural descriptors only if search space is large.
